saySample.text: You push through the doors into open air. Haven grounds — tents, a fire pit, worn paths. The world is that way.
You break ground behind the hall — bed 1 of 2, turned and ready. Sow seed to start a crop.
You break ground behind the hall — bed 2 of 2, turned and ready. Sow seed to start a crop.
You catch fragments by the fire — A woman, maybe 60s telling A man, maybe 50s, with calloused knuckles about himself. The retelling is already better than the event.
💧 A man, maybe 50s, with calloused knuckles returns with water: +2 clean.
🚶 A person, maybe 60s, with a wiry build is back — found A man, maybe 50s, with calloused knuckles.
💧 A man, maybe 60s returns with water: +4 clean.
💧 A man, maybe 50s, with weathered hands returns with water: +3 clean.
💧 A woman, maybe 30s, with a nervous tic returns with water: +2 clean.

"Hey." A man, maybe 50s, with weathered hands settles near you, not too close. "Day one. Everyone's pretending they're fine. ...Can we talk? Just talk — like people used to." (Talk to A man, maybe 50s, with weathered hands.)
Recipe: Bark armor (Level 1). You have seen bark armor. Plates of bark laced together, worn like a shell.

🛡️ Dawn at Haven. By the fire hangs an old bark cuirass, split at the seam — somebody's grandfather wore this into the treeline and came back. The shape of it is clear: bark plates laced overlapping like shingles, vine cord. Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.
⚠ STARVING: health and energy falling. You went to bed on an empty stomach.
Village meal: +1200 kcal, +1L water from the communal pantry. (Half ration — they don't trust you yet.)
A woman, maybe 40s and A man, maybe 20s are comparing scars like trading cards.
🔍 A crouches over a flooded flat of grass-like stalks hung with grain heads, studying it a moment before moving on. (1/3 looks)
A woman, maybe 30s, with a nervous tic came back with 759 kcal of something edible. The pantry breathes.
A person, maybe 30s came back with 317 kcal of something edible. The pantry breathes.
Hannah and Lucas lingered over the fire together.
Raj and Consuelo lingered over the fire together.
📓 Journal: the man in his 50s, with weathered hands taught the man in his 40s Herbal Medicine.
— DAY 2 DAWN — The world wakes. Animals are active.
Consuelo Zamora reads the sky: clear tomorrow, cold.
A person, maybe 30s will work the garden once each day while at Haven. Other orders take priority.
You step into the Haven hall.
📋 A woman, maybe 60s — 🎣 Fish. (a natural — good pick) They'll report back by next part.
📋 A man, maybe 50s, with calloused knuckles — 🎣 Fish. They'll report back by next part.
(Talking costs a little energy — 10 kcal a conversation. Small talk is cheap; going deep costs time, not more food.)
Hunger gnaws. The pack is thin — work the green, haul it back, get it named at camp. That's the whole game.
"Elena," they say, touching their chest. "I'm Elena." You'll remember that.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Elena).
...and then it lands: A man, maybe 20s speaks 🇺🇸 English. A few shared words. Gestures. Patience.
"Theo," they say, touching their chest. "I'm Theo." You'll remember that.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Theo).
You eat Dried meat and Trail mix (1400 kcal).
It's barely dawn. The day is yours — sleep is for later.
No risky water to boil.
Drank clean water.
A person, maybe 60s, with a wiry build shakes their head. "Ask someone who trusts you." (Trust too low.)

🌿 A person, maybe 30s checks the pantry before heading out — the shelves are full, ~7 days of fresh on hand… leaves the harvest standing and turns to the wood run instead. The pantry can't take more; the wild will keep.
🪵 A person, maybe 30s hauls back 6 wood. The pile grows. (16 logs now.)
💧 A woman, maybe 60s returns with 10L of creek water. Risky until the hearth boils it.
🪨 A man, maybe 50s, with calloused knuckles pries 1 stone loose from the creek bed. The building pile grows. (1 stone now.)
You catch fragments by the fire — A woman, maybe 30s, with a long braid telling A man, maybe 40s about A man, maybe 50s, with calloused knuckles. It's barely the same story now. That's what fires do.
A person, maybe 60s, with a wiry build heads out for water. "The well won't fill itself."
A man, maybe 50s, with weathered hands heads out for water. "Thirst doesn't negotiate. Going."
A woman, maybe 30s, with a nervous tic heads out for water. "Off to the well — back with a full skin."
Iron cold. Even the ticks are shelved.
— MIDDAY — Honest work hours. Heat builds.
You wait. The light changes. Nothing asks anything of you.
